keyVerseText: And they shall fall one upon another, as it were before a sword, when none pursueth: and ye shall have no power to stand before your enemies.
rootMeaning: The root of תְּקוּמָה (tᵉqûwmâh) is קוּם (qûwm), which carries the fundamental idea of rising up, standing, or establishing. This root encompasses notions of endurance, confirmation, and the ability to rise or be raised. Thus, the literal sense of תְּקוּמָה goes beyond a simple physical stance to include the power or capacity to stand firm and resist, reflecting strength and perseverance inherent in the concept of standing.
usageInScripture: The word תְּקוּמָה appears only once in Scripture, specifically in Leviticus 26:37, where it is translated as 'power to stand.' This consistency in translation highlights its focused meaning related to the ability or strength to stand firm, especially in the context of opposition or adversity. The singular occurrence underscores its particular significance in describing a state of vulnerability when that power is lost.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding תְּקוּמָה as the power to stand enriches our grasp of human frailty and divine sovereignty. It reminds believers that true strength to endure opposition comes not merely from human effort but ultimately from God’s sustaining power. This word points to the spiritual reality that without God’s enabling, one can have no lasting stability before adversaries. Christ, who perfectly embodies steadfastness and victory, is the source of our true תְּקוּמָה, empowering believers to stand firm in faith amidst trials.
keyVerseReflection: Leviticus 26:37 states, 'And they shall fall one upon another, as it were before a sword, when none pursueth: and ye shall have no power to stand before your enemies.' Here, תְּקוּמָה vividly conveys the loss of strength and stability in the face of judgment. It emphasizes the complete inability to resist or endure opposition without God’s blessing, illustrating the dire consequences of turning away from Him and the vulnerability that results when the power to stand is withdrawn.
